_comment: The wise old tree of the Glimmerwood (docs/plan-grandfather-knot.md): offers and turns in TWO quests in a row. clear-the-grove (six deadwood, simple), then the-sleeping-roots (offered only once the first is completed; it carries the story: his roots hum the wood calm, three sleep, so the young treants have turned angry) whose turn-in row is the only source of EntanglingRoots. Standing talkable-NPC shape (hermit.json): faction townsfolk, collisionLayer 97 (NOT Action), role creature + speed 0, xpFactor 0. Body radius 0.7 = twice a normal NPC (PO ask); interaction.range 2.4 keeps the usual reach from his bark. ⭐ EACH STAGE HAS ITS OWN WORDS: briefs and the deadwood reminder are stage-gated nodes, and every step row sits on root, where the show-rule leaves exactly the walkable one. ⚑ TEXT HAS A VOICE (PO 2026-10-03, the plain-text exception): slow, smug and kind, thinks in seasons, calls you little walker (plan §3.4). The player rows stay plain. All values [PLACEHOLDER].
name: GrandfatherKnot

lines: Come back in about a century, little walker. Tell me how your journey went.
Ah. A little walker. You move so... quickly.

options.text: Do you have a task for me?

grants.line: Take this, little walker. Slowly. There is no hurry.

options.text: The root by the stream is awake.

grants.line: Hm. That one was awake already. Or it is now. Try the one by the stones, to the south.

options.text: The root by the stones is awake.

grants.line: Was it warm? No? Then it was asleep. Good. The last one lies east, where the wisps gather.
There. Do you feel it? You have walked my roots end to end.
They know your hand now. Ask them to hold, and they will.
The young ones will not calm in a day. A tree's day is long. Take this as well.

lines: My grove is choked with deadwood, little walker. Clear it for an old tree?

grants.line: Good. I will wait. I am good at waiting.

lines: Six heaps will do. The rest can wait a winter.
The young trees of this wood have grown angry, little walker. Have you met them?
My roots run beneath all of it. Through them I hum the wood to rest. But three of my roots have fallen asleep.
Wake them for me. One sleeps by the stream, to the west. Lay a hand on it.

grants.line: Good. West, to the stream. I will be here.

lines: West, little walker. The root by the stream.
South. The root by the stones. Take your time. I do.
East, where the wisps gather. The last one. Probably.
